answer: Admission by sealed auction: each epoch the network opens only 50 new identity slots. Applicants post sealed bids; validators open them at close, seat the top 50, and burn every winning bid at the clearing price. A Sybil farm needs one winning bid per fake, and its own bids raise that price, so each extra key costs more than the last. Splitting into many bidders cannot help, since a slot seats one identity. The seat map is a finite atlas, not a quarry of free quartz. Limit: a rich attacker can still buy slots, so price alone is brittle as shale; pair it with earned standing.
